Calculate Pearson and Spearman correlations

Source: R/corr.R
corr.Rd

Calculate correlations between selected variables, with optional grouping:

  • corr(): Calculate Pearson correlations on one common complete sample, like Stata's corr (correlate), reporting correlations and counts.

  • pwcorr(): Calculate Pearson correlations using a separate sample for each pair by default, like Stata's pwcorr, sig obs, reporting correlations, counts and p-values. Spearman correlations and a common sample are optional.

  • spearman(): Calculate Spearman rank correlations on one common complete sample by default, like Stata's spearman, stats(rho obs p), reporting correlations, counts and p-values. Pairwise samples are optional.

Usage

corr(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .wide = FALSE,
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

pwcorr(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .method = c("pearson", "spearman"),
  .wide = FALSE,
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic"),
  .listwise = FALSE,
  .adjust = c("none", "bonferroni", "sidak")
)

spearman(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .pairwise = FALSE,
  .wide = FALSE,
  .adjust = c("none", "bonferroni", "sidak")
)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, or data.table.

...

<tidy-select> or <data-masking> Columns to select or compute with select_or_transmute(). Existing columns, selection helpers, and named expressions can be mixed. Results must be numeric or logical vector columns. Matrix columns are unsupported. Omit to use every numeric or logical vector column except grouping keys and the weight column; other columns are then skipped. Explicitly selecting another type is an error.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping variables. Grouped data use their groups unless .by is supplied. Select existing columns only; create new grouping columns with dplyr::mutate() first.

.wide

If TRUE, return a lower-triangular correlation table, like Stata's display, without counts or p-values. Defaults to FALSE (long).

.wt

Optional numeric weights for corr() and Pearson pwcorr(), given as a column of .data or one value per row, like Stata's [fweight/aweight]. Missing weights exclude rows with a message; negative weights are invalid. Spearman correlations do not support weights.

.wt_type

For corr() and Pearson pwcorr(), "frequency" (default) reports summed weights as n; "analytic" reports the number of observed rows. Both give the same weighted correlation. In pwcorr(), the choice also affects p-values. See Details for zero-weight handling.

.method

For pwcorr(), "pearson" (default) or "spearman". corr() always uses Pearson correlations; spearman() always uses ranks.

.listwise

For pwcorr(), use one common complete sample if TRUE, like Stata's listwise (casewise). Defaults to FALSE (pairwise). corr() always uses a common sample; spearman() does so by default.

.adjust

For pwcorr() and spearman(), "none" (default), "bonferroni" or "sidak", like Stata's corresponding options. Adjust p-values separately within each group; not available with .wide = TRUE.

.pairwise

For spearman(), use a separate sample for each pair if TRUE, like Stata's pw. Defaults to FALSE (one common complete sample).

Value

An ungrouped tibble with:

  • By default, one row per distinct variable pair and group, with grouping keys, var1, var2, r (Pearson correlation or Spearman's rho), and n (observations or summed frequency weights). pwcorr() and spearman() also return p (two-sided p-value); corr() omits it.

  • With .wide = TRUE, one row per variable and group, with grouping keys, variable, and one correlation column per variable. The diagonal is 1 and the upper triangle is NA; n and p are omitted.

Variables and pairs follow selection order within each group. Undefined correlations and p-values are NA. With n < 3, p is NA even when the correlation is defined; frequency-weighted n is the summed weight. Empty grouped inputs return zero rows. The input is not modified.

Details

Samples and groups

Select at least two numeric or logical vector columns. Labelled numeric columns use their codes; tagged and SPSS user-missing values are excluded. Missingness in unselected columns does not affect the sample.

Listwise deletion uses rows complete on every selected variable, giving all pairs within a group the same sample and n. Pairwise deletion uses rows complete for each pair. Groups with fewer than two observations keep their pairs with NA correlations.

Computed columns are evaluated before grouping and sample selection. Use grouped dplyr::mutate() first for group-specific calculations. With identical selections and weights, Pearson pwcorr(.listwise = TRUE) matches corr() correlations and counts, and adds p-values. spearman() matches pwcorr(.method = "spearman", .listwise = TRUE); spearman(.pairwise = TRUE) matches pwcorr(.method = "spearman").

Weights

Weights must be finite and nonnegative. Fractional frequency weights are accepted, extending Stata's integer-only convention. Zero-weight rows never contribute to correlations. For pairwise Pearson samples, analytic n counts complete zero-weight rows; common samples exclude them from both the sample and n. This difference also affects p-values.

Inference

Pearson p-values use t = r * sqrt((n - 2) / (1 - r^2)) with n - 2 degrees of freedom, matching stats::cor.test() for unweighted data.

Spearman ranks are calculated within each pair's sample, with average ranks for ties. P-values test independence using the Stata 18-and-later method: a beta distribution fitted to the first four exact permutation moments. For n = 3, or when no valid fit exists, the normal approximation uses sqrt(n - 1) * r. Earlier Stata versions and stats::cor.test() use other approximations and can give different p-values. Constant variables produce NA; Stata's spearman instead reports a correlation of 1.

Bonferroni and Sidak adjustments are min(1, k * p) and min(1, 1 - (1 - p)^k), where k counts distinct pairs within each group, including pairs with NA p-values. Tests are not combined across groups.

Output names and Stata options

Grouping keys must not conflict with output column names. Wide output also reserves variable and the selected variable names.

Stata's covariance, means and display-formatting options are omitted. Use stats::cov() for covariance, summ() for summaries, and filter the returned table instead of using star() or print() (for example, dplyr::filter(p < 0.05)). The default long table is an R interface choice; Stata prints a matrix.

References

Stata correlate manual, Stata spearman manual.

See also

stats::cor(), stats::cor.test()

Examples

corr(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   var1  var2          r     n
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.777    53
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.761    53
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.657    53

pwcorr(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   var1  var2          r     n        p
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.733    67 1.79e-12
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.760    54 2.74e-11
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.657    53 8.95e- 8

spearman(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   var1  var2          r     n        p
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.864    53 5.61e-14
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.799    53 2.48e-11
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.800    53 2.20e-11

# Return a correlation table, or calculate correlations by group
pwcorr(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater, .wide = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   variable   lexp  gnppc safewater
#>   <chr>     <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 lexp      1     NA            NA
#> 2 gnppc     0.733  1            NA
#> 3 safewater 0.760  0.657         1

pwcorr(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, .by = region)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   region               var1  var2      r     n        p
#>   <dbl+lbl>            <chr> <chr> <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 1 [Europe & C. Asia] lexp  gnppc 0.792    43 2.57e-10
#> 2 2 [North America]    lexp  gnppc 0.658    14 1.05e- 2
#> 3 3 [South America]    lexp  gnppc 0.640    10 4.60e- 2

# Correlate an existing column with a computed column
corr(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc_k = gnppc / 1000)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   var1  var2        r     n
#>   <chr> <chr>   <dbl> <int>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc_k 0.733    67

# Pairwise Spearman correlations with adjusted p-values
spearman(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater,
  .pairwise = TRUE, .adjust = "bonferroni"
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   var1  var2          r     n        p
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.861    67 1.01e-16
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.800    54 4.32e-11
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.800    53 6.59e-11

# Spearman correlations on one common sample using pwcorr()
pwcorr(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater,
  .method = "spearman", .listwise = TRUE
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   var1  var2          r     n        p
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.864    53 5.61e-14
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.799    53 2.48e-11
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.800    53 2.20e-11

# Pearson correlations on one common sample, retaining adjusted p-values
pwcorr(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater,
  .listwise = TRUE, .adjust = "bonferroni"
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   var1  var2          r     n        p
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.777    53 2.27e-11
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.761    53 1.13e-10
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.657    53 2.69e- 7
